findings.description: `deadExports` is stored flat across adapters. In a TS+Python repo whose Python side never declared vulture, TS always fills `deadExports` while Python gaps on every run, so `holdsFigure` returns true and `pup audit` refuses forever. That is the "never-measured metric blocks for good" case this delta was meant to remove.
findings.body:
**In a TS+Python repo without vulture, `pup audit` can never refresh the baseline.**

`holdsFigure` decides per *metric*, but dead code is measured per *adapter* and merged into one flat array. `measureDebt` (`src/core/debt.service.ts` L56-69) records a gap for each adapter that returns `unavailable`. It still sets `debt.deadExports` as soon as any other adapter measured:

```ts
if (capability === 'dead code') return debt?.deadExports !== undefined;
```

Here is how it plays out:
- `ADAPTERS = [typescriptAdapter, pythonAdapter]` and `detectAdapters` keeps every adapter that matches (`src/adapters/adapter.registry.ts` L7-13). A TS+Python repo therefore runs both, which is the case decision 72 names.
- The TS `deadCode` always returns a `DeadExport[]` (`src/adapters/typescript.adapter.ts` L237-245). That means every stored baseline has `deadExports`.
- Python returns `{ unavailable: 'no vulture declared in …' }` whenever vulture isn't declared (`src/adapters/python.adapter.ts` L293-295). That means every audit has a Python `dead code` gap.
- `holdsFigure(previous.debt, 'dead code')` is true, so `unmeasured` is never empty. `persistBaseline` is never called again, and both `pup audit` and `pup audit --sweep` exit 1 with "Baseline kept" on every run.

At the merge base, such a repo refreshed normally. The refusal protects nothing here, because the stored figure never contained Python's share.

The baseline does not record which adapters contributed, so `holdsFigure` cannot tell "Python measured before and failed now" from "Python never measured". Possible fixes:
- store the ids of the adapters that measured dead code (e.g. `debt.deadCodeAdapters`) and check `gap.adapterId` against them;
- or keep the previous run's gaps and block only on a gap that is new.

The new test only covers the single-adapter coverage case. A two-adapter dead-code test would pin this down.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/dcfe5d326f474da816a5c1e677954a254251b36f/src/core/audit.service.ts#L126-L160

findings.description: On the refusal path, `printBaselineTail` still prints the fresh, unstored measurement as `debt baseline: …`, and its findings say "The gate will skip that stage until it is fixed". Each gap reason also prints twice (findings on stdout, `refuseKept` on stderr). So the output describes a baseline that was not stored, right above "Baseline kept".

`holdsFigure` spells out 'coverage' and 'dead code' as bare string literals instead of reusing `DEAD_CODE`/`COVERAGE` from `src/core/debt.service.ts:37-39`. If those names are renamed there, it silently falls through to `return true` and the audit refuses for good, which is the block this function exists to prevent.
The decision 38 amendment says "the drift still prints", but only a plain audit prints it. `pup audit --sweep` calls `refuseKept()` (src/cli/index.ts L1931) before printing any drift.

The test comment "The drift still prints: the measured metrics moved…" repeats the WHY in the `src/cli/index.ts` comment at L1981-1982. Keep it once, at the call site; the `build    PASS` assertion already shows the intent.
